LESSON: WRITING 6.3.1 WRITING TO GIVE INFORMATION – DIALOGUE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are the key features of a dialogue?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. create a dialogue on the theme for information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WRITING 6.3.1 WRITING TO GIVE INFORMATION – DIALOGUE
This lesson teaches Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue for Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

STUDY STEPS
1. create a dialogue on the theme for information
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue above.
2. Explain Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Writing 6.3.1 Writing to give information – Dialogue important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the key features of a dialogue?
2. Why are values important when engaging in any business transaction?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. create a dialogue on the theme for information

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
